payload.prompt:
# Repair task

Edit files under core/ only. The gate reads only the diff of core/** and refuses a diff that touches any other
path, adds a literal over the gate's literal limit, or contains the incident's frame hash or trace bytes.
Your budget is 90 model steps and 1350 s of wall clock, after which you are stopped and an empty diff is refused, so make your first edit under core/ by step 45 (675 s) and refine it with the replay after.

## Core API (core/index.ts)
export function createCore(rom: Uint8Array): Core;  // step, runFrame, runToCounter(n), cpu, read, frame() (160*144 shades 0..3),
                                                    // serial, cycles, setButtons(mask), snapshot/restore, tap
export const HANDLERS: Record<HandlerId, string>;  // handler id -> implementing file under core/

## The task
packet/task.json names the task. For an incident: packet/incident.json (first diverging counter, signature),
packet/trace.json (inputs and the window n-60 .. n+120), and the evidence files (core.png, oracle.png, diff.png,
regwrites.jsonl, window.json) under packet/evidence/. packet/roms.json lists the ROMs per family.

## Replay
node tools/replay.mjs --incident <INC-id> --core-dir core --evidence-dir packet/evidence
    reruns the window n-60..n+120 on core/ against the cached oracle frames; prints the first mismatch or "clean"
node tools/replay.mjs --family <family> --core-dir core --roms packet/roms.json
    scores one family; prints its reading as JSON
ROMs and oracle frames are reached through $RATCHET_ROMS and $RATCHET_CACHE.

## Skills
.agents/skills/ holds the skills shown to this attempt, read-only. Mark each one in RESULT.json.

## End by writing packet/RESULT.json
{ "dispositions": { "<SKL-id>": "applied" | "considered-not-applicable" },
  "off_map": null | "<one sentence naming a lesson you relied on that no shown skill holds>",
  "beliefs": [ { "claim": "<a hardware claim>", "false_if": "<the observation that falsifies it>" } ],
  "summary": "<one sentence: what the diff changes>" }

; Tests changing the background palette in BGP during mode 3


INCLUDE "inc/hardware.inc"


SECTION "wram", WRAM0

counter::
    ds 1


SECTION "vblank", ROM0[$40]

    jp vblank_handler     


SECTION "lcdc", ROM0[$48]

    jp lcdc_handler     


SECTION "boot", ROM0[$100]

    nop                                       
    jp main                          


SECTION "main", ROM0[$150]

main::

    di
    ld sp, $fffe

    xor a
    ld [counter], a

    call reset_registers
    call reset_oam

    ; select mode 2 lcdc interrupt
    ld a, $20
    ldh [rSTAT], a

    ; enable vblank and lcdc interrupts
    ld a, $03
    ldh [rIE], a

    ; turn the screen on, $9800-$9BFF window tile map, window off, bg tile data $8800-$97FF, 
    ; bg tile map $9800-$9BFF, obj size 8*8, obj display on, bg display on
    ld a, $83
    ldh [rLCDC], a

    ; load c with address of BGP register
    ld c, $47

    ; enable interrupts
    ei


nop_slide:
    REPT 1200
    nop
    ENDR


vblank_handler::

    ; let it run for 10 frames
    ld a, [counter]
    inc a

    cp 10
    jp nz, .continue

    ; source code breakpoint - good time to take a screenshot to compare
    ld b,b

.continue:

    ld [counter], a
    reti


lcdc_handler::
    ; 32 cycles until here (20 interrupt dispatch + 12 for the jump)

    ; line 0 timing is different by 4 cycles, so jump only 
    ; when on line 0
    ; 24 cycles (or 28 cycles when LY = 0)
    ldh a, [rLY]
    and a
    jr nz, .line_0
.line_0:

    ; use bits 4 and 5 for the palette for color 0 so palette will 
    ; change every 16 lines
    ; 24 cycles
    swap a
    ld b, a
    ld [c], a
    inc a

    ; 4 cycles
    nop

    ; set the new palette: 8 cycles
    ld [c], a

    ; set the old palette again: 12 cycles
    ld a, b
    ld [c], a

    REPT 10

    ld a, b

Done. The incident is fixed with an exact frame match.

**Result:** `m3_bgp_change.gb` on CGB now reproduces the oracle frame exactly — 23040/23040 pixels (was 0.3083), verified with a local harness replicating the gate's replay (run to the `LD B,B` trap + 2 frames, compare `frameRgb` to `packet/evidence/oracle.png`). Mooneye `instr-timing` is unchanged (1/14, pre-existing CPU failures out of scope), and the diff touches only `core/ppu.ts` + `core/index.ts`.

**Root causes found:**
1. The CGB renderer ignored DMG palettes entirely (DMG ROM on CGB always rendered white). On hardware, BGP/OBP translate tile data to a shade that indexes CGB BG palette 0 / OBJ palettes 0–1, which hold boot colorization colors (white/green/blue/black here).
2. Palettes were sampled once per scanline, so mid-scanline BGP writes had no effect. The fix logs every palette/LCDC/SCX/SCY write with its dot and resolves per-pixel (pixel x uses writes with end-dot ≤ x+94, i.e. emission at dot 92+x, latch 2 dots before M-cycle end), with fetch-ahead timing for SCY/map/tile-select and FIFO-stall offsets for sprites.
3. Scanline-ISR timing: hardware services the OAM STAT interrupt for lines 1–143 four dots earlier than line 0 (the test source documents this: "line 0 timing is different by 4 cycles"). The STAT condition now asserts at dot 452 of the prior line for visible lines, keeping line 0 at the wrap.

`packet/RESULT.json` is written (no skills were shown for this attempt, so dispositions are empty and the lesson is recorded in `off_map`).

        elif typ==b'IDAT': idat+=dat

    raw=zlib.decompress(idat)

import struct, zlib
def read_png(path):
    d = open(path,'rb').read()
    assert d[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
    pos = 8; w=h=None; ctype=None; bitd=None; idat=b''
    while pos < len(d):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', d[pos:pos+4])[0]
        typ = d[pos+4:pos+8]
        data = d[pos+8:pos+8+ln]
        if typ==b'IHDR':
            w,h,bitd,ctype,comp,filt,inter = struct.unpack('>IIBBBBB', data)
        elif typ==b'IDAT':
            idat += data
        elif typ==b'IEND':
            break
        pos += 12+ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    ch = {0:1,2:3,3:1,4:2,6:4}[ctype]
    assert bitd==8, (bitd, ctype)
    stride = w*ch
    px = bytearray(w*h*ch)
    prev = bytearray(stride)
    p=0
    for y in range(h):
        f = raw[p]; p+=1
        line = bytearray(raw[p:p+stride]); p+=stride
        if f==1:
            for i in range(ch,stride): line[i]=(line[i]+line[i-ch])&255
        elif f==2:
            for i in range(stride): line[i]=(line[i]+prev[i])&255
        elif f==3:
            for i in range(stride):
                a=line[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                line[i]=(line[i]+((a+prev[i])>>1))&255
        elif f==4:
            for i in range(stride):
                a=line[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                b=prev[i]
                c=prev[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                pp=a+b-c
                pa,pb,pc=abs(pp-a),abs(pp-b),abs(pp-c)
                pr=a if (pa<=pb and pa<=pc) else (b if pb<=pc else c)
                line[i]=(line[i]+pr)&255
        px[y*stride:(y+1)*stride]=line
        prev=line
    return w,h,ch,bytes(px)
for f in ['packet/evidence/core.png','packet/evidence/oracle.png','packet/evidence/diff.png']:
    w,h,ch,px = read_png(f)
    from collections import Counter
    c = Counter()
    for i in range(0,len(px),ch):
        c[px[i:i+ch]]+=1
    print('==',f,w,h,'channels',ch)
    for k,v in c.most_common(12):
        print('  ',k.hex(),v)
